candidates.title: The Resend webhook copies every email's recipient, subject and click link into a collection nobody reads
evidence: webapp:server/utils/jobOutcomes.ts:52 subject 'How did it go with ${otherSide}?' (the site's name for the company's question)
resend.com/docs/webhooks/emails/clicked: data has to, from, subject, click.link, click.ipAddress, click.userAgent
cmd: grep -rn growth_campaign_events server scripts -> only the writer (resend-webhook.ts:50)
candidates.today: For every customer email, the Resend webhook stores the recipient's address and the whole event payload: subject, sender and, for a click, the link, IP address and browser. Subjects include a site's name in the company's outcome question. A click on a site email is its signed private job link. Nothing reads these documents, nothing deletes them, and withdrawal does not touch them.
candidates.should: The webhook keeps only what it must: suppressions for unsubscribe, complaint and permanent bounce, plus the delivery status of the outbox row by Resend email id. No address, subject or link is stored in an observation table.
candidates.proposal: In resend-webhook.ts stop writing growth_campaign_events and growthCampaigns. On delivered, bounced or complained, set deliveredAtIso or bounce on the captureOutbox row whose stored Resend id matches (see O-16). Keep recordEmailSuppression. Ask the owner to approve a one-off delete of the 403 existing documents.
candidates.user_result: A site's email, name and private link no longer sit in a forgotten table; the owner can see which emails bounced.
candidates.risk: Outreach campaign stats go (the campaigns are retired). Deleting existing documents is a production write the owner must approve.
candidates.requirement_source: nobody (growth studio era; the file comment says it 'outlived the growth studio')

also_reported.title: The email delivery webhook keeps every recipient address for a retired growth-campaign system

webapp:server/routes/resend-webhook.ts:84-99 (suppression on bounce/complaint/unsubscribe: the part that matters)
also_reported.today: Each Resend delivery event for any Blueprint email, including site and company job emails, is stored with the recipient address and the whole payload under "growth campaign events". No campaign has been written since June.
also_reported.proposal: One PR: keep the recordEmailSuppression branch; delete the growth_campaign_events and growthCampaigns writes. Owner: purge the 403 stored events and 58 campaigns.

candidates.journey_step: O.5 Personal data in observation stores
candidates.title: Sent outbox rows keep the site's email, signed job link and name in plain text forever, also after withdrawal
evidence: webapp:server/utils/taskLifecycleNotifications.ts:53-82 (bodies end with the private job url)
webapp:server/utils/jobOutcomes.ts:52,154-158 (outcome question subject names the other side)
cmd: grep captureOutbox in websiteCaptureWithdrawal.ts, websiteCaptureDeletion.ts, accountDeletion.ts -> no match
candidates.today: After a site email is sent, its outbox row keeps 'to' (the site's email), the subject and the body. The body contains the signed private job link, and anyone holding that link acts as the site. The company's outcome question keeps the site's name in its subject. The two introduction emails are cleared on send; the other eleven kinds are not. Withdrawal and account deletion leave these rows alone.
candidates.should: Once a row is sent or cancelled, it keeps only kind, status, times, attempts and the Resend id. Rows of a withdrawn job are cleared at withdrawal.
candidates.proposal: Extend clearedIntroductionDetails in captureOutbox.ts to every kind: clear subject, body and replyTo on sent or cancelled, and keep 'to' only as a hash for deduplication. Add a withdrawal step that clears every row of the request. Ask the owner to approve a one-off backfill of the existing sent rows.
candidates.user_result: A site's private link and email stop living in a queue table after the email has gone.
candidates.risk: Debugging a delivered email loses its text; the builders can regenerate it. A suppression check that reads 'to' must use the hash.
candidates.requirement_source: nobody (introduction kinds were cleared on purpose; the rest were missed)

candidates.title: The new-job email says nothing about the job
candidates.today: Every new-job email reads 'A site has posted a new job. Open it to see the job packet and respond.' No job type, place or readiness. A company must sign in to learn whether it is relevant.
candidates.should: Subject and first line name the job type and country (and state if the owner allows): 'New job: Move materials, United States'.
candidates.proposal: Build the subject and body from the card's category title and country, which every approved company already sees on the card.
candidates.user_result: A company triages from its inbox; fewer wasted sign-ins; fewer unsubscribes.
candidates.risk: Words must stay non-identifying; use only the fixed category and country.
candidates.requirement_source: package E4 'Nothing about the site' (category and country are not about the site's identity)

candidates.title: No email when the simulation becomes ready, and companies approved later never hear of open jobs
candidates.today: The send happens once, when a job is first listed, only to companies that have already accepted the Terms signed in. An approved company not yet signed up is skipped for that job forever. Nothing tells anyone when the simulation package appears.
candidates.should: One email when a job becomes Ready to test; a newly signed-in company sees a one-line 'N open jobs' on its first visit (it already sees the list).
candidates.proposal: Add a second idempotent outbox row per company (key robot_team_job_ready:<job>:<company>) queued when storedCompanySimulation first exists; reuse the same dispatch gate.
candidates.user_result: Companies learn the moment they can answer 'Tested it: can do'.
candidates.risk: One more email per job; must respect the same opt-out.
candidates.requirement_source: doctrine: once a job's simulation exists a company downloads it and tests

candidates.title: The packet gives the country only, while the application asks for cities and states
candidates.today: Job page and cards say 'United States'. The job stores city, state and postal code. A company cannot tell whether a job is in its area without emailing.
candidates.should: The job shows state and country (never the city or address).
candidates.proposal: Return the decrypted state with the country in countryOf and show 'Texas, United States'; add it to the sharing statement wording if the owner requires.
candidates.user_result: A company decides 'in our area or not' from the packet.
candidates.risk: State is coarse but more than today; the sharing statement does not list region, so the owner decides.
candidates.requirement_source: privacy hard stop (no address); the country-only rule itself is from package E3

candidates.title: Cards in the job list look alike
candidates.today: Cards show a regex-picked category ('Move materials') and the country. Several identical cards; the lead must open each job.
candidates.should: Each card shows the site's sentence, already redacted for companies, under the title.
candidates.proposal: Add the redacted sentence (companyJobPage's sentence) to the card payload and render one line of it.
candidates.user_result: A lead picks the relevant job from the list without opening each.
candidates.risk: The card is the widest surface; the same redaction must run (it already does for the page).
candidates.requirement_source: package E2 anonymised listing

candidates.title: The application asks three questions nothing reads, and hides the one field the check needs
candidates.today: Six required fields, three free text (jobs, robots, region). No rule reads jobs or robots; the region check compares against countries so 'Texas and Oklahoma' never matches. The website, the signal for 'website matches email', is optional and collapsed.
candidates.should: Four fields: name, work email, company, company website (required, visible).
candidates.proposal: Remove workWanted, robot and region from the form and schema (keep reading old records); make website required; drop the region check.
candidates.user_result: Applying takes a fraction of the typing; the approver sees the two signals that matter.
candidates.risk: The owner may want robots to judge borderline applicants; can ask in reply. Could come back.
candidates.requirement_source: nobody (no rule reads them); website: guard robotTeamAccessFit.ts

candidates.title: After approval: a password, a second Terms agreement and a details review before the first job
candidates.today: Approval email, link, a screen with password, Terms box and collapsed name and company, then Create account. Terms are 'agreed' on the application too, though that tick never counts.
candidates.should: The email-bound link signs the company in; first visit shows one 'I agree' press; nothing else.
candidates.proposal: Redeem the invitation as a sign-in link (custom token) without a password; show CompanyTermsPrompt on first visit; delete the details review and the application's Terms line (replace with a Privacy notice).
candidates.user_result: One fewer screen, no password, one Terms agreement instead of two.
candidates.risk: Recovery without a password relies on 'Email me a new link', which exists. The signed-in Terms press must stay.
candidates.requirement_source: planner G1 (signed-in agreement); password: nobody

candidates.title: A declined or waiting applicant is never told anything
candidates.today: Only approval is emailed. The 'in review' and 'declined' screens need a signed-in account, and an applicant cannot have one. Silence means no, not yet, or unread.
candidates.should: One 'not yet' email on decline, and a reply-by date on the receipt.
candidates.proposal: Queue a fixed 'not yet' email on decline (same outbox path as approval); delete the unreachable status screens.
candidates.user_result: A company knows where it stands.
candidates.risk: Reverses the owner's 2026-11-19 direction.
candidates.requirement_source: owner direction 2026-11-19 (only approval emailed)

candidates.title: Nobody can see how long approval takes, and nothing reminds the owner
candidates.today: One Slack message on a new application; no timer, reminder or measurement of applied-to-decided time, the slowest human link here.
candidates.should: A daily line to the owner listing applications older than N days; the duration shown on the review page.
candidates.proposal: Add an ops alert for robotTeamAccess with status applied and appliedAtIso older than N days.
candidates.user_result: Companies are approved sooner; the owner sees the queue.
candidates.risk: An alert the owner ignores is noise; one line a day.
candidates.verify_how: Run the robotTeamAccess duration aggregate listed in the report.
candidates.requirement_source: doctrine: Blueprint approves a company once

candidates.title: The simulation package opens only in USD tools and does not explain the success rule

candidates.proposal: Change nextAction text per answer (Interested/Tested can do: the meet line; Need more details: the site is asked; Not a fit: nothing more).
candidates.user_result: The company knows what to expect.

candidates.title: Approving a company takes a Slack bell, a sign-in, a page in another design, a confirm box and a note box
evidence: webapp:server/routes/robot-team-access.ts:88-91 (only bell: notifySlackRobotTeamAccessApplication, if a webhook is set)
candidates.today: A company applies. If a Slack webhook is set, Slack gets a message with a link. The owner opens it, signs in, finds the card on a dark 'Partner applications' page that says partners, robot team, early access and site tasks, presses Approve, ticks a browser confirm ('I reviewed the team's capabilities, task fit, and prerequisites'), answers a browser prompt for a note, and only then is it saved. Production has one company record in total.

Delete the confirm and prompt dialogs. Use the doctrine's words on the page.

candidates.title: An email outage over 36 hours cancels introductions for good, and the site cannot ask again
evidence: webapp:server/utils/captureOutbox.ts:201-206 a row refused past that age becomes failed
webapp:server/utils/jobIntroductionGate.ts:169-174 a failed company email cancels the introduction, clears both sides' details and voids the billable event
webapp:server/utils/jobIntroductions.ts:118-121 'One cancelled at dispatch is not made again: its emails' keys are spent' -> already_introduced
webapp:server/utils/jobCompanies.ts:530 canIntroduce is false for a cancelled pair; client/src/lib/siteIntroductions.ts:21 'This introduction could not go ahead. We did not give them your details.'
candidates.today: If Resend refuses for 36 hours (quota, outage, revoked key) or the web process that sends email is down that long, every introduction queued then is cancelled. The site reads 'This introduction could not go ahead' and the Introduce us button never comes back for that company. Nobody can redo it short of editing records.
candidates.should: A cancelled introduction caused by Blueprint's own email failure can be asked for again with the same one press.
candidates.proposal: Key the introduction emails and billable event by attempt (for example append the cancelled count), and let canIntroduce be true again when cancelReason is company_email_failed or company_email_not_sent. One PR in jobIntroductions.ts and jobCompanies.ts with tests. Keep the void on the old billable event.
candidates.user_result: The site presses Introduce us again after an outage instead of losing that company.
candidates.risk: Two billable events for one pair (one void, one recorded); the invoice must count only recorded ones, which status already says.
candidates.requirement_source: nobody for 'never again'; the void-on-failure rule comes from the introduction gate design (G3/H2) and protects money

candidates.risk: A site that closed its job gets up to three short emails; each email has five answers, and a final answer ends the questions.

candidates.title: One worker heartbeat covers seven loops; a stuck send or outcome loop goes unnoticed
candidates.journey_step: B.1 Job sent to companies; A.9 follow-up
evidence: webapp:server/worker.ts:47-59 seven loops, one heartbeat (workerHeartbeat.ts:20, stale after 5 min)
webapp:server/utils/jobAutoSend.ts:131-140 and jobOutcomes.ts:174-183 a 'running' guard with no timeout: one hung await stops that loop forever
webapp:server/utils/jobAutoSend.ts:121 writes automationState/companyAutoSendCursor.updatedAtIso; grep in betaOpsMonitor.ts -> nothing reads it
webapp:server/utils/jobOutcomes.ts:134-167 the outcome sweep records nothing about its runs
candidates.today: The worker writes one heartbeat for the whole process. If the automatic send, the outcome questions, the withdrawal or the deletion loop hangs or keeps throwing, the heartbeat stays fresh and nothing alerts. The send loop records when it last ran but nobody reads it.
candidates.should: Each loop writes 'last finished at' and the ops monitor alerts when one is overdue.
candidates.proposal: Have each start*Worker write opsHeartbeats/<loop> after each finished pass (one helper), and extend checkWorkerHeartbeat to read all seven with their own intervals. Add a per-pass timeout (Promise.race) so a hung pass releases 'running'.

candidates.risk: Six more small Firestore writes per minute.
candidates.requirement_source: doctrine 'No person at Blueprint stands between a site's video and an introduction' (the loops must run unattended)

candidates.title: The core journey test checks introduction and follow-up emails only as queued, never as sent
evidence: webapp:e2e/site-answer-journey.spec.ts:134-135,359-367 reads outbox rows (kind, to, body) through a test route

It never runs the sender, so it cannot see that the site's 'Meet the company' row is still held, that Reply-To is replaced by hello@ at send time (A-01), or that a send fails. The test passes while the email a person receives is wrong.

This test will fail today on Reply-To, which is the point.
candidates.user_result: The next Reply-To-style bug is caught before a site sees it.
candidates.risk: Adds a few seconds to the journey.

candidates.title: Model runs store the site's job text unredacted in agentRuns, and withdrawal leaves it
evidence: webapp:server/agents/runtime.ts:825-848 (only lanes with persist_content 'redacted' are digested)
candidates.today: For brief reading, coverage review, video evidence and robot-fit ranking, each run row keeps the task input and the model's output word for word. The input includes the site's own description of its job. These rows are kept for cost and debugging, and withdrawal does not purge them.
candidates.should: Every lane that reads site text stores lengths and a digest, as the follow-up lane already does. Cost and timing fields stay.
candidates.proposal: Mark site_task_brief_reading, capture_coverage, site_video_evidence, capture_video_privacy and robot_fit_ranking persist_content: 'redacted' in their task definitions. Ask the owner whether to backfill existing rows.
candidates.user_result: A withdrawn site's job text is not left behind in a cost log.
candidates.risk: Replaying an old run for debugging is no longer possible (REDACTED_CONTENT_NOT_REPLAYABLE already handles that refusal).
candidates.requirement_source: nobody for keeping the text; cost telemetry needs only usage fields

candidates.title: A billable event lacks what an invoice needs: legal entity, billing contact and the Terms version
evidence: webapp:server/utils/billableEvents.ts:16-26 (fields: kind, requestId, companyId, atIso, priceUsd, status)
webapp:server/utils/robotTeamEarlyAccess.ts:37-53 (company: name, email, company, website, robot, workWanted, region; no legal entity or billing contact)
cmd: grep -rn 'legalEntity|billingContact|legalName' server client/src -> only Blueprint's own COMPANY.legalName
candidates.today: Each introduction records the job, an internal company id and the press time. Blueprint knows no company's legal name or billing email. The Terms version the company accepted is overwritten at its next acceptance, so after a Terms change nobody can show which version it held.
candidates.should: When the owner decides how to charge, each event already names the company's legal entity, a billing email and the Terms version in force, frozen at the moment of the introduction.
candidates.proposal: (1) Ask for legal entity name and billing email once, on the approval or accept-Terms step. (2) In buildIntroductionBillableEvent, copy companyLegalName, billingEmail, termsVersion and privacyVersion (from termsAcceptance) and statementVersion onto the event at create. No price, no payment code.
candidates.user_result: The owner can bill the first introduction the day he picks a model, without chasing companies for details.
candidates.risk: One more field for an approved company. It touches money, so it is the owner's call when to ask.
candidates.requirement_source: doctrine 'each introduction is recorded as a billable event'

candidates.journey_step: O.2 What the owner can observe
candidates.title: No total of jobs, sends, answers, introductions or billable events anywhere, and no export
evidence: webapp:server/utils/jobConsoleData.ts:34,112-152 (25 per page, no count, no filter)
webapp:client/src/types/jobConsole.ts:16-26 (list row: id, sentence, phase, standing, receivedAt only)
candidates.today: To learn how many jobs came in, the owner pages through /admin/jobs 25 at a time (76 jobs is 4 pages) and counts by hand. Sends, answers, introductions and billable events can be seen only by opening each job. Nothing exports billable events.
candidates.should: One daily email gives the totals and this week's movement for each step, the jobs waiting on Blueprint, and the introductions made. One admin route exports billable events as CSV.
candidates.proposal: Add a read-only daily digest in the worker (leader-leased, one email to CONTACT_TO), built from count() aggregates on inboundRequests, companySends, companyResponses, introductions and billableEvents. Add GET /api/admin/billable-events.csv. Then delete the intake-notice Slack duplicate and growth_events (O-13).
candidates.user_result: The owner sees in one message whether the loop works and what needs him.
candidates.risk: Low; read only. Collection-group count queries may need an index.
candidates.requirement_source: doctrine (the owner must see billable events); IW-07

candidates.title: A billable event looks the same before the company has the site's details as after
evidence: webapp:server/utils/jobIntroductions.ts:151 (event created at the press with atIso = requestedAtIso)
webapp:server/utils/jobIntroductionGate.ts:162-167 (send path releases the site row; the event is not touched)
webapp:server/utils/jobIntroductionGate.ts:85-87 (company row 'dispatching' or 'unknown' holds with no end)
candidates.today: The event is written 'recorded_no_price' when the site presses. It turns void only if the company's email is cancelled or definitely fails. If that email sits 'unknown', or if neither side has a usable email so no row is made, the event stays 'recorded' with no proof the company ever got the details.
candidates.should: An invoice counts only introductions that were made: the event carries madeAtIso, set when the company's email is marked sent.
candidates.proposal: In companyIntroductionEmailEnd's sent branch, also merge { madeAtIso } onto the event (the event is already read there). The daily digest and the export count only events with madeAtIso.
candidates.user_result: The owner never bills a company for an introduction it did not receive.
candidates.risk: Small: one more write in an existing transaction. Tests pin 'changes one only to void it' (money-introduction-billable-events.test.ts:311), so that test must change.
candidates.requirement_source: money hard stop

candidates.title: The public funnel is not measured, and growth_events (1,247 docs) is written by retired code and read by nothing
evidence: webapp:server/utils/growth-events.ts:45-78 (writer stores current_url, referrer and user.email as sent)
cmd: grep -rn growth_events server client/src scripts -> writer only
candidates.today: After consent, the site sends page views and one start-form event to /api/analytics/ingest. That persists only if a flag is on (unknown). Separately, capture-era 'proof motion' code stamps growth_events. Nobody reads the collection. Video uploaded, shown to companies, answered and introduced exist only as job records, and nothing turns them into a funnel.
candidates.should: The funnel is read from the job records themselves (Firestore aggregate 4) in the daily digest. Nothing else is collected.
candidates.proposal: Delete growth-events.ts, analytics-ingest.ts and its route, the logGrowthEvent calls in inbound-request.ts and internal-pipeline.ts, and the 54 unused analyticsEvents. Ask the owner to approve deleting the 1,247 documents.
candidates.user_result: One honest funnel from real records; about 1,000 fewer lines.
candidates.risk: Visit counts are lost if the ingest flag is on today; the server request log still holds page loads.
candidates.requirement_source: nobody (capture-era proof motion)
